consensus_summary: Works are human deeds/actions serving as the outward fruit, expression, and evidence of inward spiritual state or allegiance (good works as fruit of faith/grace; evil works as fruit of sin/flesh), by which persons are known and judged, though traditions differ on their precise soteriological role.
book_summary: A work is simply a deed, not a synonym for obedience; it becomes obedience or disobedience only relative to a command, while context separately identifies wages, duty, or faith made visible.
consensus_core_identification: deeds as outward fruit/evidence of inner faith or sin
book_core_identification: a deed (distinct from obedience), with any obedience/wages/duty/faith-visible role supplied only by context
boundary_disagreement: Consensus builds fruit/evidence and often obedience into the primary sense of works; the book excludes automatic synonymy with obedience and treats faith-made-visible, wages, or duty as contextual rather than definitional, narrowing the loaded cases admitted by default.
material_contradiction: None on the bare referent (deed/action); the divergence is boundary and loading, not replacement of the central category.
rationale: Both identify works as deeds/actions. The consensus core loads that referent with fruit/evidence-of-inner-state (and frequently with obedience) as primary across traditions. The book preserves the deed referent but materially tightens precision and extension by denying synonymy with obedience and relocating wages/duty/faith-visible aspects to context alone. This is refinement by narrowing and reclassification of boundary cases, not core contradiction or novelty.
strongest_objection: The many fruit, judgment, and good-works-as-evidence texts that dominate the consensus (Matt 7; Jas 2; Eph 2:10; Rev 20) make the evidential loading feel definitional rather than merely contextual, so the book's sharper separation may under-read those passages.
